blindSummary: Trans visitors here face serious risk on paper. The criminal-offences statute criminalises sodomy (10 years, plus corporal punishment on paper — unenforced in recent years) and also criminalises males "impersonating a female" while soliciting — a direct trans-expression statute on the books. Against that: there is a visible indigenous trans-feminine community occupying a traditionally supported third-gender role (its local name translates as "like a lady"), and a widely attended trans beauty pageant (profiled by a major foreign newspaper in 2024); family and religious-community networks are devout but not systematically violent, and no documented recent prosecutions.
blindOutOfScope: The male-impersonation statute is on the books but unenforced.
blindTangential: The sodomy statute (10 years, unenforced) is a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the "impersonating a female" provision is trans-specific but scoped to soliciting.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the criminal-offences statute outlaws same-sex activity (maximum 10 years, no recent enforcement evidence) and criminalises male 'impersonation' of a female for an 'immoral purpose'; no legal gender recognition; intersex people unprotected; traditionally supportive culture around an indigenous feminine third-gender role (its name translates as 'like a lady'), though rising conservatism threatens this.
